critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 809 lines — well past the 700-line threshold. Split into modules: routers/tariffe.py, routers/clienti.py, routers/lavori.py, routers/pdf.py, services/calcoli.py (calcola_alaggio/varo/motore_labor/ricambi), models/*.py.

calcola_alaggio/varo boundary: '<=5' means 5m boats get forfait but 5.01m goes to per-metro (5.01*25=125.25 > 90). This is a discontinuity where a marginally-larger boat pays MORE than the forfait despite being longer — acceptable business rule but worth documenting; some cantieri prefer max(forfait, perMetro) to avoid jumps.

ClienteForm.jsx SheetFooter sticky bottom-0 does not clamp to viewport in tall forms — should either wrap SheetContent in `flex flex-col` and use `flex-1 overflow-y-auto` on the body + non-sticky footer, OR add `max-h-screen` with proper column layout. Users hitting the tallest form (existing cliente + lavori section) must scroll to reach Salva/Annulla.

Ricambi are ALWAYS billed even when potenza_motore=0 (backend calcola_ricambi doesn't gate on HP), so a 'no engine' cliente still gets girante+olio+filtro+candele+termostato+olio_piede (~215€ by default). If the intent is 'no motor -> no maintenance charge at all', gate ricambi on potenza_motore>0 too. Otherwise the UI hides the breakdown when HP=0 (good) but the backend still returns and stores costo_manutenzione_motore = ricambi_totale, which will appear in the PDF/table.
Tariffe.jsx save() coerces empty/invalid inputs to 0 silently (`Number(t[k]) || 0`) — user can accidentally wipe a tariff by clearing the input. Should validate and warn.
PDF endpoint hardcodes 'PORTOMARE' brand and orange/navy palette — no configurability; consider extracting brand config for white-labeling.
calcola_ricambi uses `nc * t.costo_candela` with nc from int(numero_candele or 0) — a negative input would produce negative ricambi (no clamp). Add max(0, nc) guard.
Cliente model default `numero_candele=4` / `numero_termostati=1` — reasonable, but ensure UI form shows these defaults for a new cliente (verified: it does).

rca_of_the_issue: During test authoring, I hit a race condition: pytest-xdist loadscope splits tests across workers by class; when TestTariffeSchema.test_put_tariffe_updates_new_fields (setting motore_labor_40_150hp=333) ran on worker gw1 in parallel with TestCalcolaCosti.test_mid_range_hp_40_150 (asserting manodopera=320) on gw0, the shared tariffe backend state caused the calc test to see the mutated value. Fix: consolidated all tariffe-related classes into one class TestTariffeAndMotore so loadscope pins the whole suite to a single worker, plus an autouse function-scope fixture resetting tariffe to defaults before every test. All 26 tests now pass consistently across parallel runs.
